title: Consolidate app-wide layering into one canonical z-index scale (#178)
body:
Closes #178.

## What changed

Every app-wide z-index magic number now reads from one named scale,
`src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/layer/z_layers.js`. 15 raw literals → 1 documented
exemption (`public/index.html`, static boot-shell CSS that cannot import JS).

| tier | value | who |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTENT_RAISED` | 10 | local accents |
| `SCROLL_OVERLAY` | 500 | scrollbar thumb overlay |
| `APP_CHROME` | 1000 | title bar |
| `APP_CHROME_TOP` | 2000 | side menu |
| `MODAL` | 3000 | blocking dialogs |
| `TOAST` | 4000 | notifications |
| `TOOLTIP` | 5000 | tooltip, explorer label ghost |
| `POPOVER_BLOCKER` | 6000 | popover click-outside catcher |
| `POPOVER` | 7000 | context menu, color picker panel |
| `DRAG_GHOST` | 8000 | explorer drag ghost |
| `TOP_PROGRESS` | 9000 | global progress bar |
| `BOOT` | 2147483647 | boot overlay |

Each tier's position is justified in the module header by a real scenario, not
by taste, and each justification has a matching invariant test. The contract
test asserts *orderings*, so values can be retuned freely as long as every
scenario still holds.

## Three deviations from the issue text

**1. The issue's scale is missing tiers.** It puts everything above `MODAL`
into one `POPOVER` rank. PR #192 (already in `dev`) established, and
`explorer.test.js` regression-tests, `MODAL < TOOLTIP < POPOVER` — flattening
those would reintroduce the exact bug #192 fixed.

**2. The issue is stale on the explorer ghost.** It says the ghost is at
`999999` and should drop to `CONTENT_RAISED(10)`. On `dev` it is already
`10000`, deliberately: Explorer renders *inside* `memory_inspect_modal`,
`theme_editor`, and `recipe_list`, so pushing it below `MODAL` would let a
modal hide its own rows' hints.

**3. The issue's `TOAST > POPOVER` ordering is wrong** — see below.

## Landing spot: `BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/layer/`, not `SERVICEs/`

33 of the 62 z-index-bearing files live in `BUILTIN_COMPONENTs`, a layer that
today imports `SERVICEs` only for runtime behavior (buses, bridges), never for
constants. Adding ~10 primitives→services edges would turn it from a leaf into
something hanging off the system-access layer, and mini_ui — the upstream these
components were ported from — has zero such imports, so a component that gained
one could not be ported back.

The singular directory name matches mini_ui's `layer/`, which also holds a
`layer_stack.js` owning the *behavioral* dismiss stack (top layer, Escape,
outside-click). **PuPu has not ported that** — `modal.js:47`,
`context_menu.js:53`, and `tooltip.js:805` each wire their own Escape listener,
with no shared stack. The name reserves the spot; the docs record the debt.

## Bugs fixed on the way

- **toast tied with modal.** Both at `9999`, so which painted on top depended
  on portal insertion order. A save-confirmation toast landing behind the modal
  that triggered it is invisible UX breakage.
- **color picker's blocker tied with modal.** Same tie. Its own test is titled
  *"above a modal"* — intent documented, held by luck.
- **three files independently hardcoded `10000`.** Two meant "tooltip tier",
  the picker meant "interactive popover". They now say which.

## Two defects caught by adversarial review, after the first push

**`TOAST` was placed above `POPOVER`** (following the issue's ordering), which
silently reversed pre-migration behavior where context menu (99999) always beat
toast (9999). This is reachable in production: `toast.error()` from
`use_chat_stream` gets `Infinity` duration, and the toast pile sets
`pointerEvents:'auto'` across its whole bounding box deliberately. A lingering
error toast overlapping an open context menu eats the click, and the menu's
outside-mousedown handler reads that as an outside click and **silently closes
the menu instead of running the item**. Fixed: `TOAST < TOOLTIP < POPOVER`.

**The picker's blocker and panel were collapsed onto one value.** Before, panel
`10000` > blocker `9999`. `theme_editor` renders a column of ColorPickers with
no focus trap and the popover never takes focus, so Tab+Enter can open a
second; tied, the second instance's transparent full-viewport blocker paints
over the first's panel and closes the wrong picker. Fixed with
`POPOVER_BLOCKER`.

Review also caught a **false claim I had written in three places** (that
`layer_stack.js` already existed in PuPu — I had read mini_ui's copy while the
shell was still in that repo) and **two holes in the guard itself**: it scanned
line-by-line so `zIndex:\n  9999` slipped through, and it exempted itself
file-wide. Both fixed and re-verified by injection.

## Ordering audit

All 91 before/after pairs were compared exhaustively. 28 orderings change:
10 are the deliberate un-tying of modal/toast/blocker (all `9999`), 8 involve
`variable_picker` (dead code boxed inside `overflow:hidden`), and the rest are
intended semantic corrections. No unaccounted flips remain.

One deliberate new tie: picker panel and context menu are both `POPOVER`. An
open picker's blocker intercepts the right-click first, so they cannot coexist.

## Verification

- frontend **317 suites / 3147 tests** green (baseline before this branch:
  315 / 3127 — the delta is exactly this branch's new tests)
- electron **30 suites / 514 tests** green
- production webpack build succeeds; the scale appears in the bundle as
  `CONTENT_RAISED:10,SCROLL_OVERLAY:500,APP_CHROME:1e3,…` and every old magic
  number (9999/10000/99999/999999/2048/2049) is gone from the output
- guard verified to actually bite, twice: injecting `zIndex: 4242` and the
  split-across-lines `zIndex:\n 7777` both fail it with the exact file:line

## ⚠️ Still needs human eyes

Automated tests cannot see paint order. Before merging:

1. right-click a sidebar chat → hover a truncated title → **title stays under
   the menu**
2. open chat memory (memory-inspect modal) → hover a truncated row → **ghost
   appears above that modal** ← most at risk from this change
3. settings → appearance → open a color picker → **above the modal, clickable**
4. trigger a toast while a modal is open → **now above it** (intended change)
5. leave an error toast up, then open a context menu under it → **menu wins**
6. drag a chat/folder → ghost above content, reorder still commits
7. cold start → boot overlay covers everything
8. **scroll any long list and confirm the scrollbar thumb is visible** — this
   overlay dropped from 9999 to 500 and is used in 40 places

## Out of scope (recorded, not fixed)

- `dnd/context.js:90` — @dnd-kit's `DragOverlay` defaults to `999` with no
  `zIndex` pass-through in our wrapper, so a dragged item there can fall behind
  overlays. Needs a prop; deserves its own issue.
- `top_progress_bar` is mounted nowhere, so its constant has no observable
  effect. Restoring `<TopProgressBar />` is a product question.
- `variable_picker` needs a portal to work at all.
- Visual order and behavioral (dismiss) order are still two independent
  systems; see the debt note above.

## Unrelated commit in this branch

`da631d8d` carries CTO/architect review records for the codex
context-memory-v2 migration. They landed here because those agents were
dispatched from the same session and the main checkout has 209 uncommitted
paths nobody should touch. Drop it if you'd rather it go elsewhere.

title: fix(explorer): keep the truncated-label ghost under menus and dismiss it on press
body:
## 症状

Explorer 行标签被截断时,hover 会浮出显示完整标签的 ghost。它有两个独立缺陷:

1. 点开 modal 后不会消失,一直悬着
2. 会盖在 context menu 和 modal 前面

## 根因(两个症状 = 两个独立根因)

**层级**:ghost 写死 `zIndex: 999999`,比 modal(9999) 和 context menu(99999) 都高一个数量级。库内通用 `tooltip/tooltip.js` 用的是 10000,explorer 这个值是个离群魔数。

**生命周期**:`clearOverflow` 只挂在 mouseleave 和 scroll 上。点击行打开 modal 时指针仍停在该行,**mouseleave 永远不会触发**,所以 ghost 一直挂着。

## 修复

`zIndex: 999999` → `10000`。这个值两边都是刻意的:

- **高于 modal(9999)**:Explorer 会被用在 modal *内部*(`memory_inspect_modal.js`),压到 9999 以下会让 modal 遮住自己行的提示
- **低于 context menu(99999)**:ghost 是被动提示,绝不该盖住可交互菜单

`handleMouseDown` 里加 `clearOverflow()`,覆盖左键(开 modal)和右键(开菜单)。调用放在 `shouldSkipRowDragStart` 早返回**之前**——一旦按下,交互已开始,提示就该让位,哪怕这次按下不会启动拖拽。

未动 1949 行拖拽跟随 ghost 的 999999:拖拽与右键菜单互斥,且未报告该症状。

## 验证

先写测试见红(4 failed,报错直接打印出 `z-index: 999999`),再改实现。

- `explorer` 套件 **15/15** 通过,含 10 个原有用例(拖拽 ghost、trailing mousedown 不启动拖拽等未受影响)
- 消费方回归(side-menu / memory-inspect / theme_editor / recipes_page):**34 套件 / 187 测试**全绿

新增 5 个用例锁定两条契约,包括"在 600ms 延迟窗口内按下后,定时器到期也不得再冒出 ghost"这个边缘情况。

其中一条断言 `zIndex > 9999` 是**保护性**的——防止后来者把层级压得太低而破坏 modal 内的用法。

title: Harden SQL migration and release durability
body:
## What changed

- Makes SQLite the durable authority for settings, chat state, provider credentials, toolkit preferences, computer-use preferences, token usage, and custom MCP icons while preserving safe legacy fallback during migration.
- Encrypts provider credentials through Electron `safeStorage`, removes secret-read IPC paths, serializes writes, and keeps rollback/retry behavior atomic.
- Handles missing or failing macOS Keychain storage with a session latch plus persisted retry cooldown, preventing repeated `PuPu Key` prompts and allowing legacy credential fallback.
- Adds coordinated renderer/main-process quit draining so pending settings, consent changes, local beta state, reset operations, chat drafts, and session bundles are durable before shutdown.
- Adds an idempotent guarded chat recovery journal so stale journal replay cannot overwrite newer SQLite state and quota/size failures synchronously fall back to SQL.
- Restricts the test API to E2E environments, hardens navigation/origin handling, and adds same-userData restart coverage.

## Why

The SQL migration had multiple release-blocking durability and security gaps: secrets could remain tied to legacy authority, Keychain failures retried on every boot, immediate quit could outrun async persistence, and a stale or oversized chat recovery journal could block shutdown or regress newer SQL data.

## User impact

- Existing users migrate without losing settings or chat state.
- Missing Keychain storage no longer causes repeated prompts every launch.
- Immediate quit/restart preserves pending drafts and settings mutations.
- Provider credentials remain encrypted at rest when Keychain storage is available and fail closed without exposing plaintext over IPC.

## Validation

- Deterministic release gate: PASS
- Frontend: 313 suites / 3,086 tests passed
- Electron: 152 suites / 1,468 tests passed
- Python backend: 963 tests passed, 3 skipped, 64 subtests passed
- MCP registry, production web build, license/notices, and Electron E2E smoke: PASS
- Full local fake-model soak: 21.1 minutes, 3 parallel root agents, 96 tool calls per agent, no page errors or forbidden log findings
- macOS arm64 unsigned DMG/ZIP build: PASS
- Packaged `.app` isolated launch/close smoke: PASS
- Security review: no remaining P0/P1 findings

## Release notes

The generated macOS artifacts are unsigned and not notarized. Real provider/Ollama/workspace smoke, Windows/Linux install checks, and the paid live-model matrix remain separate release steps.

Moves Computer Use configuration out of Settings and into the **plugins panel**, per CEO direction: capabilities all live in one place, and this establishes the **per-plugin settings page contract** that future toolkit customization (per-tool write confirmations, OAuth management, …) will reuse.

- **Installed → Built-in section** gains a synthetic "Computer" row (mouse icon, read-only On/Off status pill from server truth, always visible, participates in search). Not in the MCP catalog — same synthetic-entry precedent as the chat attach menu; backend untouched.
- **Row click opens a detail overlay** (existing `openDetail` mechanism, new `plugin_settings` kind) hosting the exact same `ComputerUseSettings` component — toggle, one-time consent, macOS permission badges. **UI moved, vessels untouched**: `settings/computer_use/` directory has zero changes; `enable_controller` remains the renderer's single call site (grep-test still passes unmodified).
- **New `plugin_settings_registry.js`** — the generic contract: `toolkitId → {Component, labelKey, icon}`. One entry today (`builtin.computer`); MCP per-tool permission panels register here later (exact-id keys now, `source:` fallback reserved as a future extension).

### Trust partition

Computer sits in the Built-in section with the builtin badge, physically separated from third-party MCP entries; its detail page renders **no TRUST_CONFIG vocabulary** (verified/community/needs_review is store trust language) and no install/delete/approve affordances.

### Security

All eight Gate-B invariants re-confirmed unaffected (component remounted, module untouched; status pill is read-only and fail-closed to Off; backend/IPC/localStorage untouched; `boot_sync` stays mounted in App.js). Deliberately avoided the hero/discover/categories/detail files under active development — the only shared touch is a minimal additive branch in `plugins_shell.js`.

title: feat(computer-use): last-mile attach path — settings nav panel + per-chat Computer entry + capability from status
body:
## Summary

Closes the **last-mile gap** in the Computer Use enable path (#183): with the master switch on, there was no way to actually attach the tool from the real chat UI — the sidecar mounts `builtin.computer` only when a request's toolkits include it, and nothing in the renderer ever sent it (the e2e passed because QA injected toolkits via test-api, masking the gap; found by the CEO asking "why can't I see it").

Three slices (CEO-decided UX: per-chat opt-in entry, not auto-mount — the security-warning system prompt stays out of chats that didn't attach the tool):

1. **Settings panel promoted to first-class** — `ComputerUseSettings` moves out of the dev-only subpage into the main settings nav (after Memory, grouped with the agent-capability pages). All 11 locales get the nav label.
2. **Per-chat "Computer" entry in the chat toolkit menu** (attach panel): visible only when the master switch is on; greyed with a hint when the session model doesn't support computer use; checked → `builtin.computer` rides the existing toolkits payload (no new storage). Synthetic entry — verified it survives every catalog-assuming render path as an opaque id.
3. **`GET /computer-use/status` exposes `supported_model_prefixes`** — the pupu-llm-expert-authored capability list moved (verbatim, with its authority comment) from `unchain_adapter` into the `computer_use_flag` leaf module; the route serves it so the frontend never duplicates the list.

## Review

- **pupu-dev-chat-core** reviewed the attach-panel changes (its surface): opaque-id passthrough, Select multi-value preservation, streaming/session-switch consistency, hook refresh pattern — LGTM; its one SHOULD-FIX (stuck disabled selection after switching to an unsupported model) is fixed via client-side reconcile: when the entry is definitively unselectable (switch off / bridge gone / unsupported model), `builtin.computer` is auto-stripped through the normal setter. Tri-state resolution guards against stripping during the async status load.
- BUILTIN `use_select` disabled semantics untouched (shared primitive).

## User path after this PR

Settings → Computer Use → toggle on (one-time consent) → chat toolkit menu → check "Computer" → talk to a supported Anthropic model (opus-4-8 / sonnet-4-6 / …).

## Test status

- Backend: **854 passed / 3 skipped** (+1 status field test)
- Electron: **121 passed** (untouched)
- Frontend: **2014 passed / 273 suites** (+33 vs dev baseline: visibility tri-state, capability greying, reconcile scenarios, panel relocation, locale keys)
- ESLint on changed files: zero warnings

## Not in this PR

- User-facing **release remains blocked** on the screenshot-injection A/B eval + security final sign-off (tracked; asset pack ready).
- Full i18n for the three chat-menu strings (en-only, falls back to English; nav label is translated in all locales).

title: feat(computer-use): Gate B user-writable enable path (settings toggle + consent + runtime override)
body:
## Summary

Adds the **user-writable enable path** for Computer Use (Gate B slice): a settings toggle that — after a one-time informed-consent gate — turns the computer-use tool on/off at runtime, no sidecar restart required.

Until now the feature flag (`PUPU_COMPUTER_USE`) was env-var only (dev-side, Gate A). This PR wires the full user path:

```
settings toggle → requireComputerUseConsent() → computer_use_enabled_store (localStorage, versioned)
  → window.unchainAPI.setComputerUseEnabled → IPC "unchain:set-computer-use-enabled"
    → electron main → authorized POST /computer-use/config (loopback + x-unchain-auth)
      → sidecar runtime override → mounted on the next chat request
```

**Note: this exposes the toggle in dev builds only in practice — the user-facing release is still blocked** until the screenshot-injection A/B eval passes and security gives the final Gate B release sign-off (tracked separately).

## Design decisions (pupu-architect, CTO signed off)

- **Runtime override as primary, spawn env as belt-and-braces**: electron main caches the desired state, re-pushes after sidecar crash-restart, and mirrors it into `PUPU_COMPUTER_USE` on respawn. No restart, no stream interruption; user's explicit OFF beats a dev env ON.
- **Red line preserved**: the mount funnel's flag gate never reads request options — the flag stays server-side authority (renderer-compromise cannot widen it).
- **Flag copies converged**: `unchain_adapter` and `memory_factory` (screenshot sanitization) now delegate to a single `computer_use_flag` leaf module — the tool gate and transcript hygiene can no longer drift apart.
- **Fail-closed everywhere**: cold start, crash-restart window, corrupted localStorage record, version mismatch, failed re-push — worst case is always "stays off".
- **Consent invariants**: decline → zero writes, zero pushes; boot re-sync re-validates consent before pushing true; renderer has a single `setComputerUseEnabled` call site, enforced by a grep-style test.

## Slices

| Slice | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | dev-backend | `computer_use_flag.py` leaf module, converged private copies, `POST /computer-use/config` (strict `{enabled: <bool>}`, 401/400 hardened) |
| B2 | dev-electron | IPC channel + parity manifests, main service (POST, tri-state desired cache, ready re-push, spawn env), preload boundary tightening |
| B3 | dev-settings | `computer_use_enabled_store` (anti-corruption reads), bridge facade, settings toggle (server-truth display state, pending/failure states), headless boot-sync host |

Plus one post-e2e fix: `setComputerUseEnabled` now returns `ok:true` (dead `ok` contract found by QA).

## Test status

- Backend: **853 passed / 3 skipped** (+20 new; flag priority, endpoint hardening, sanitize-follows-flag)
- Electron: **121 passed** (+8 new; strict boolean, crash-restart re-push, cache-null no-op)
- Frontend: **1981 passed / 271 suites** (+26 new; consent-decline zero-effect, store anti-corruption, boot-sync tri-state, call-site uniqueness)
- ESLint on changed files: zero warnings (CI lint gate pre-checked)

## In-app e2e (real machine, real model)

All PASS: fail-closed baseline → real-vessel enable (renderer→IPC→main→POST, no curl forgery) → funnel mount + claude-sonnet-4-6 screenshot round-trip (model accurately described the live screen) → on-disk transcript contains zero raw base64 (media_id references only) → disable takes effect next message → `kill -9` sidecar → auto-respawn restores enabled state without renderer involvement.

## Security review

pupu-security-expert audited the full diff (27 files) against the eight design invariants — all verified at file:line, **merge to dev = GO** (audit record in `.claude/agent-memory/pupu-security-expert/computer-use-gate-b-enable-review.md`). Remaining before the user-facing release: screenshot-injection A/B eval + final release sign-off.

title: feat(computer-use): M2 — GUI screen control (screenshot + mouse/keyboard), flag-off by default
body:
## Summary

Adds **Computer Use (M2)** to PuPu: a built-in first-class tool that lets a capable Anthropic model control the user's real desktop — screenshots + mouse/keyboard injection — through PuPu's existing tool pipeline. GUI screen control only (browser automation was the deferred M1); Anthropic-first.

**Feature-flagged OFF by default.** The flag (`PUPU_COMPUTER_USE`) has *no setter anywhere* in the shipped app (env-var only, dev-side), so merging this to `dev` exposes nothing to users. This was verified and signed off by the security review as **Gate A (flag-off, merge to dev) = GO**.

## What's in here

**Sidecar "hand" (`unchain_runtime/server/computer_control/`)** — new self-contained module: `mss` screenshot + downscale + coordinate/scale-map (Retina DPR=2 handled), `pynput` injection backends (macOS CGEvent / Windows SendInput / Linux X11 XTest), platform capability probing with Wayland degrade-to-screenshot-only.

**Toolkit + adapter wiring** — `ComputerToolkit` (Anthropic `computer_20251124` predefined tool + `computer-use-2025-11-24` beta), mounted via a new `builtin.` branch in `_build_selected_toolkits` (additive; existing `mcp.`/generic branches untouched). Mount requires **all three**: flag on AND model-capable AND not a subagent run.

**Security (SEC-001 gate-B items, all code-complete):**
- **F1** — injection actions (click/type/key/scroll/drag/move) forced through server-side confirmation; read-only actions (screenshot/wait/cursor_position) exempt via fail-closed allowlist.
- **F9** — computer tool never mounted in recipe-subagent runs (no confirmation channel there).
- **F2** — screenshot prompt-injection: system-prompt security warning injected only when the computer tool is mounted; structurally zero-pollution for non-computer sessions.
- **F2 consent** — one-time informed-consent modal (reuses existing `AgreementModal`, no new panel), own localStorage key, versioned.
- **F3** — screenshot base64 stripped from on-disk session transcript (wraps `JsonFileSessionStore`; deep-walks messages + checkpoint; base64 → media reference, TTL-bounded).
- **F6** — pynput LGPL-3.0 written source-offer added to third-party notices generator + release gate for future copyleft deps.

**Media + status** — `GET /chat/tool-media/<id>` (TTL, loopback + token + unguessable id), `GET /computer-use/status` (capabilities + permissions for the settings panel).

**Frontend** — read-only settings panel (Screen Recording / Accessibility badges + system-settings deep links via main-process allowlist), status bridge, consent modal. Dev-visible only.

Requires the unchain library changes **already merged to unchain `dev` (`52854bd`)**: S0 rich tool result (image blocks reach the model) + S1 provider-native predefined tools. The shipped sidecar must resolve an unchain build that contains S0/S1, or the computer tool will not function (it degrades: flag-off = inert, so no breakage on `dev` today).

- unchain S0/S1: 855 passed / 0 regression (dual-signed: llm-expert + CTO).
- sidecar server suite incl. all computer-control tests: 591 passed / 2 skipped / 0 regression.
- frontend: 1392 passed (consent store + modal + panel).
- Real-hardware smoke: screenshot capture + coordinate invariant (declared == returned == PNG dims) verified on Retina; injection smoke intentionally not run (never moved the cursor).

- **QA**: screenshot-injection A/B eval + in-app end-to-end need an Anthropic API key + integrated environment — deferred to post-merge.
- **Gate B (flag ON to users)** is still BLOCKED until QA passes; a user-writable enable switch + flag-write/sidecar-config path is a separate pre-release slice (dev stays env-var).
- **Known accepted limitation (CEO-accepted)**: typed text reaches the transcript via model tool_call arguments (relies on OS disk encryption); not gate-B blocking.
- **Wayland**: injection is second-phase (degrades to screenshot-only + explicit "not supported").
- **Overlay cursor visualization**: fast-follow after F1 baseline (feasibility spiked; screenshot-feedback-pollution risk retired via `setContentProtection`).

title: #34 hide suggested models
body:
## Summary

Hides OpenAI and Anthropic model groups from the chat model dropdown and hero-screen suggested model chips when no API key is configured for those providers. When a user saves or clears an API key in Settings, the model selector and hero chips update reactively without requiring a page reload.

- **`useChatInputModels` hook**: Reads configured provider API keys from local storage and filters out OpenAI/Anthropic model groups when no key is present. Subscribes to `subscribeModelCatalogRefresh` to react to key changes.
- **`ChatInterface` (chat.js)**: Applies the same filtering to the hero-screen suggested model chips.
- **`APIKeyInput` component**: Calls `emitModelCatalogRefresh()` after saving or clearing an API key so downstream components update immediately.

## Testing

- Added unit tests in `use_chat_input_models.test.js` covering:
  - Hides both OpenAI and Anthropic groups when no API keys are configured
  - Shows only the OpenAI group when only an OpenAI key is set
- Fixed existing tests that were broken by `resetMocks: true` in CRA's Jest config (mock implementations were being cleared before each test); corrected by setting the `readModelProviders` mock return value in `beforeEach`.
- Added a defensive `|| {}` null-check in `read_configured_providers` to guard against unexpected `undefined` from storage.
- All 4 tests in the modified test file pass; no regressions in the wider test suite.

title: Add workflow to enforce only `dev` merges into `main`
body:
Any PR targeting `main` from a branch other than `dev` should fail CI, blocking the merge.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/enforce-merge-source.yml`** — new workflow that triggers on PRs targeting `main`, checks `github.head_ref == "dev"`, and exits 1 if not
  - Scoped to `permissions: contents: read` (least-privilege)

```yaml
- name: Check if source branch is dev
  run: |
    if [ "${{ github.head_ref }}" != "dev" ]; then
      echo "❌ Only the 'dev' branch is allowed to merge into 'main'."
      exit 1
    else
      echo "✅ Source branch is 'dev'. Merge allowed."
    fi
```

## Required follow-up

Add `check-source-branch` as a **required status check** on the `main` branch ruleset — without this, the failing check won't block merges.

body:
Extends `LLM_endpoint` to support Anthropic Claude (`claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`) and Google Gemini (`gemini-1.5-flash`) via their REST APIs, with full tool calling integration using the existing `LLM_toolkit` schema.

## Changes

- **Fixed mutable default arguments** in `LLM_tool.__init__`, `LLM_toolkit.__init__`, and `LLM_endpoint.chat_completion` (changed `[]`/`{}` to `None` with proper initialization)

- **Added API key parameters** `claude_api_key` and `gemini_api_key` to `LLM_endpoint.__init__`

- **Implemented Anthropic provider** (`anthropic_fetch_response`)
  - Converts messages/tools to Anthropic Messages API format (`input_schema`)
  - Handles streaming SSE responses with `content_block_delta` events
  - Executes tool calls via `LLM_toolkit.execute` and appends results to message flow
  - 300s timeout, proper JSON parsing error handling

- **Implemented Gemini provider** (`gemini_fetch_response`)
  - Converts messages/tools to Gemini format (`functionDeclarations`)
  - Handles streaming SSE responses with `functionCall` parts
  - Executes function calls via `LLM_toolkit.execute` and appends results to message flow
  - 300s timeout, proper error handling

- **Updated provider routing** to use `elif` chain supporting `"anthropic"` and `"gemini"` alongside existing `"openai"` and `"ollama"`

## Usage

```python
# Anthropic Claude
endpoint = LLM_endpoint(
    claude_api_key="sk-ant-...",
    provider="anthropic",
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"
)
endpoint.toolkit = LLM_toolkit(tools={"calculator": calc_tool})
response = endpoint.chat_completion(messages, callback=stream_handler)

# Google Gemini  
endpoint = LLM_endpoint(
    gemini_api_key="AIza...",
    provider="gemini",
    model="gemini-1.5-flash"
)
endpoint.toolkit = LLM_toolkit(tools={"search": search_tool})
response = endpoint.chat_completion(messages)
```

Tool execution flow matches existing OpenAI/Ollama behavior: LLM requests tool → `toolkit.execute(name, args)` → result appended to message history → returned.

body:
Replaces browser localStorage with Electron main process file storage under `userData/storage/`. No migration of existing data.

## Storage Layout
```
userData/storage/
├── address_book.json          # Chat sessions metadata
├── favoured_models.json       # User model preferences
├── sections/<address>.json    # Chat history per session
└── files/<key>.txt            # Uploaded images (base64)
```

## Changes

**Electron main process** (`public/electron.js`)
- Added IPC handlers for CRUD operations on JSON files
- Storage initialization creates directory structure on app start
- Separate handlers for sections, files, and metadata

**Preload bridge** (`public/preload.js`)
- Exposed `storageAPI` via contextBridge for renderer access

**Storage abstraction** (`src/utils/storage.js`)
- New module wrapping IPC calls with error handling
- Async API matching file operations

**Data layer** (`src/CONTAINERs/data/container.js`)
- Converted all localStorage calls to async storage API
- `load_from_local_storage`, `save_to_local_storage`, `delete_address_in_local_storage` now async
- File operations (`save_input_files`, `load_saved_files`) properly awaited

**Storage UI** (`src/COMPONENTs/settings/storage_manager/storage_manager.js`)
- Updated size calculation to query filesystem via IPC
- Delete operations now remove both section JSON and associated files

**Chat component** (`src/COMPONENTs/chat/chat.js`)
- `on_input_submit` and `update_message` made async to await file saves/loads
- Message component loads files asynchronously

## Example
Before:
```javascript
localStorage.setItem(UNIQUE_KEY + "address_book", JSON.stringify(data));
const data = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(UNIQUE_KEY + "address_book"));
```

After:
```javascript
await storage.writeAddressBook(data);
const data = await storage.readAddressBook();
```

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Please migrate PuPu off browser localStorage and onto Electron-based file storage (no migration of existing localStorage data). Implement a multi-file JSON storage layout and keep the existing storage management UI.
> 
> Repo: haoxiang-xu/PuPu
> 
> Requirements:
> 1. Storage backend: Electron main process file storage under app.getPath("userData")/storage/ with this layout:
>    - storage/address_book.json
>    - storage/favoured_models.json
>    - storage/sections/<address>.json
> 2. Expose a preload bridge API (e.g., window.pupuStorage) for renderer usage. Provide methods to:
>    - getAddressBook / setAddressBook
>    - getFavouredModels / setFavouredModels
>    - listSections (list section addresses)
>    - getSection(address) / setSection(address, data)
>    - removeSection(address)
>    - getStorageStats() returning totalSizeMB and per-section size + chat_title
> 3. Renderer changes:
>    - Replace all localStorage reads/writes in src/CONTAINERs/data/container.js and src/COMPONENTs/settings/storage_manager/storage_manager.js with the new bridge API.
>    - On startup, load address_book, favoured_models, and section data from the new storage API.
>    - Save updates via the new storage API in existing useEffect/save logic.
> 4. Keep the storage management panel functional:
>    - Size calculation and list should come from getStorageStats() (not localStorage)
>    - Deleting a section should call removeSection(address) and update addressBook state
> 5. Do NOT implement any migration from existing localStorage data.
> 6. Keep functionality and UI behavior otherwise unchanged.
> 
> Please add any needed IPC handlers in the main process, update the preload script, and ensure the renderer has access to the new API without breaking context isolation.
> 


</details>
